name: Cimetidine
summary: The first H2 blocker — effective acid suppression but a potent CYP enzyme inhibitor and a major source of drug interactions.
mechanism: Competitive antagonist at parietal-cell H2 receptors, reducing basal and stimulated gastric acid secretion.

dosing.adult: Peptic ulcer: 400 mg twice daily or 800 mg at bedtime; OTC heartburn: 200 mg as needed
dosing.renalAdjustment: CrCl < 30 mL/min: 300 mg every 12 h or a longer interval

safety.pregnancy: Extensive historical use; no major teratogenicity demonstrated
safety.lactation: Excreted in breast milk; considered compatible (famotidine often preferred)
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to cimetidine or other H2 blockers
warnings: Potent CYP inhibitor (1A2/2D6/3A4) — check warfarin, phenytoin, theophylline, clozapine levels
Antiandrogenic effects at high doses (gynecomastia, impotence)
Confusion in elderly or renal impairment
monitoring: Response and warning symptoms (GI bleeding, dysphagia, weight loss)

clinicalPearls: The classic drug-interaction poster child — its CYP inhibition affects warfarin, phenytoin, theophylline, and many others
High-dose or long-term use can cause reversible gynecomastia via antiandrogen effects
bad: Polypharmacy (CYP interactions); high-dose long-term use; renal impairment without dose adjustment
